drafted_from: tool:evaluate-a-formula's own row (its words, input schema, sample runs and steps) and what its sample runs answered here; read it before relying on it
start_here: Say to your AI: "Evaluate a formula over each row of a list: read a value from the row, then run a pipeline of steps (and, or, not, equals, more than, less than, is in a list, position in a list, lower-case, contains, starts with, join, is empty, is unknown) over it", with {"binding":{"$kind":"binding","select":{"from":"self","path":["name"]},"transform":[{"op":"op:core.lower"},{"op":"op:core.contains","args":{"value":"rye"}}]},"rows":[{"name":"Dark RYE loaf"},{"name":"Scone"},{"name":null}]}. It runs tool:evaluate-a-formula and answers {"values":[true,false,null],"errors":[]}
no_lists_because: It names no list of yours: it takes its input and answers, and keeps no row.
instructions: 1. Say to your AI: "Evaluate a formula over each row of a list: read a value from the row, then run a pipeline of steps (and, or, not, equals, more than, less than, is in a list, position in a list, lower-case, contains, starts with, join, is empty, is unknown) over it", and give it binding ({ $kind: binding, select: { from: self, path: [...] }, transform: [{ op, args }], default?); rows (The values to evaluate the binding over).
2. The AI calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run, tool tool:evaluate-a-formula and its input (the worked example shows one).

3. Read what comes back: Takes a binding (select from the row at a path, or a stated literal, then a transform list of { op, args }; an argument may itself be a binding evaluated over the value the step receives) and rows.
